question: For the frozen 127 absent-ray pairs, how much selected normalized price delta is raw capability versus roster-median shift?
design: Exact selected price decomposition: actual delta minus base price, compared with ray raw normalized by the base median; residual is the median-shift component. Same 8 roots, 127 pairs and evaluator config as ray_pair_novelty_price_result.json.

summary.base_vs_semantic_normalization_type_sets: Identical {A,B,P,X} on all 8 roots; no membership-set contribution in this sample.

interpretation: Across this frozen finite sample, roster renormalization removes about one-third of the aggregate selected-type price increase relative to holding the base median fixed. It attenuates or leaves unchanged all 127 increases (101/127 attenuated). The decomposition is exact for this profile implementation and sample, not an alternative calibrated evaluator, price law or utility result.
limitations: Eight generated 6x6 classic-like roots and finite absent direct-ray pairs only.
No outcomes, search, training, calibration, post-move exposure or utility measurement.
Summed pair contributions weight each eligible type-direction pair equally and are not population-weighted.
The exposed/unexposed stratification is descriptive within these same eight roots, not an independent exposure-versus-utility test.
